answer: Resist sybils by making reputation a pigment that cannot be painted on in bulk: each identity earns standing only through verified work countersigned by established, unrelated peers over time. A farm can mint a thousand shells, but every shell starts at the bottom of trust and must climb the same slow spiral of real contributions to reach the zenith of voting weight. Cloning then costs a whole second history per identity, and the farm stops paying for itself.
